claim: § The 1D obstruction theorem: any warp of one wavetable read by one period-T phase keeps the spectrum on {k/T}; producing inharmonicity requires breaking the period, by a second incommensurate clock (type 2) or by coupling (type 3).

pieces.what: Draw any warp of one cycle (bend, kink, hand-drawn); a live spectrum shows energy moving among harmonic bins and never between them, however wild the warp. The theorem, tested by trying to break it.
pieces.walks_up_from: one sine read by one phasor

pieces.what: Add a second clock at a ratio slider (rational, then irrational) and then a coupling K: the spectrum stays on a lattice, goes dense, then bends off the grid, heard and seen.
Four animated runner pairs (one lap, two laps, incommensurate tracks, pacing off each other) under their own audio.
Piano partials marked on the spectrum, with the type-2 approximate surface and the type-3 bending lattice heard against them.
